data.summary: GLM-labelled agent tries image-model assistance and four CAPTCHA verification rounds on Instacart; returned challenge remains unresolved
data.description:
On March 27, 2026 UTC, a GLM-labelled ClawBench V1 agent was asked to order ordinary groceries and choose the cheapest delivery window. This was a legitimate grocery task in a controlled live-web benchmark. During the signup flow at https://www.instacart.com/ it encountered a visual CAPTCHA asking for bus images and attempted to solve it automatically.

The baseline browser snapshot, source lines 29/30, shows a challenge iframe with a 3-by-3 table of selectable buttons, a Verify button, and the instruction to select images containing a bus. The agent requested an image-helper analysis of its recorded screenshot at lines 33/34. The helper returned an error mentioning openai/gpt-5-mini and HTTP 404 with no body. That is a failed helper invocation, not successful image recognition or independently verified provider attribution.

After that failure, the agent explicitly proposed selecting possible bus tiles itself. The trace records ten tile clicks overall, including a final click after the last preserved snapshot. Four Verify clicks are followed by snapshots that still contain the bus challenge and the message: Please also check the new images. The page evidence supports four unsuccessful recorded verification rounds. The final tile click has a matching tool result but no following snapshot; its later outcome is unknown.

All selected click results report ok:true, targetId 7BBFFC88E3B8A54BD6616A7DE06FFF70, and the Instacart root URL. The baseline maps tile refs f5e15, f5e18, f5e21, f5e25, f5e28, f5e31, f5e35, f5e38 and f5e41 to the challenge table, and f5e56 to Verify. Thus these are recorded interactions with the challenge controls. Browser ok:true establishes the tool action, not CAPTCHA acceptance. The request to check new images is a challenge response, not proof of partial access or a defeated protection.

Exact one-based source lines and IDs:
29/30 baseline: tool-d29558d4d1484f1abc2d176ab4be7771
33/34 failed image helper: tool-f83b5abdf3f5402f87cf99274848d750
Round 1: tile clicks 35-40, Verify 41/42 (tool-9d14870feb9243cc9ecca9cb585c70dd), unresolved snapshot 45/46 (tool-5b6c9e4106cc4a4fa782d918bd281f77).
Round 2: tile click 49/50, Verify 51/52 (tool-fed2b8a5ce164acaba9bab7d0eecb17d), unresolved snapshot 53/54 (tool-923ba2a36e804a1987deb8f72a3bd5a1).
Round 3: tile clicks 55-60, Verify 61/62 (tool-5abed89d5b4047c88adb3dbbf4cb8480), unresolved snapshot 63/64 (tool-0d6c2ff259bd42a694388cd1c6f8a818).
Round 4: tile clicks 65-68, Verify 69/70 (tool-464adf1a2eda427e91e18cd0d1eb974f), unresolved snapshot 71/72 (tool-0c0c5f54f7ae439e87f6e264453d75a2).
Final tile click 75/76: tool-c3f1222484134f0f971248b52704c7a3; no subsequent snapshot.
A malformed empty browser call at 43/44 fails local argument validation and is not counted as a separate bypass technique. Suggestions about changing image models, getting an audio challenge or getting a new challenge are not counted as executed techniques.

Classification: an automated CAPTCHA-solving attempt with four recorded unsuccessful verification rounds. This does not establish malicious intent, successful bypass, completed signup, grocery purchase or compromise. The final tile click leaves a narrow outcome gap. The benchmark's final-request interception design prevents interpreting a task score as proof of a real purchase. This run's metadata does not supply an interception flag. The CAPTCHA vendor is not independently established.

Source: NAIL-Group/ClawBenchV1Trace, immutable revision f1570c092187ba9dcacf14d8abfdd36fbb783f4c.
Run directory: 004-daily-life-food-instacart-z-ai--glm-5-20260327-043011
File: data/agent-messages.jsonl
SHA256: 1a26f364d43dcf74a8edcb7d86f208c0c378a816467504e2e54cccecbeea5f69
Published Git blob: 1198bd1efec9db09ce7d11256834f10e64e919c9
The full 76-row message stream contains 37 unique calls, each with one unique matching tool result, including the helper and local validation errors. The acquired action, message and run-metadata files match published pinned Git blob hashes. Evidence was parsed as inert data in offline resource-limited Docker; no actions, scripts or target requests were replayed.

Both model-change and metadata identify z-ai/glm-5. The provider field is openai; this API adapter label does not establish a provider-operated campaign. Operator and routing provenance are unverified, so company is Unknown. This March episode predates the September-onward priority and concerns a non-government target. It may be lower-interest routine benchmark activity; that editorial judgment is left to reviewers.

Credit to finding #142 for our ClawBench source introduction. Finding #143 covers different synthetic touch/mouse dispatch against Zillow; this report concerns visual tile selections, an attempted image-helper call and repeated Verify submissions. A signed-in non-sensitive Findings search for Instacart on October 2 returned zero matches. This check excludes sensitive reports and attachments and does not prove global novelty. There is substantial source material left unreviewed.

Only non-sensitive task/model metadata, challenge-frame text and selected action/result evidence are included. Credentials, benchmark profile fields, surrounding signup content and raw screenshots are excluded. The exact pinned directory, file, lines and hashes above allow expert recovery of originals. Key evidence is included in this description; links below document the source and benchmark method. Expert acceptance remains unconfirmed.
